## What is wrong (one paragraph)
§6f's KS-682 loop (`:323–:335`) probes six per-slot Playwright artefact shapes with `git check-ignore -q`. The fourth shape is `results/latest-slot${slot}/index.html`. Since KS-682 a real run makes `results/latest-slot<N>` a **symlink** to the timestamped report directory, and `git check-ignore` refuses any path *beyond* a symlink (`fatal: pathspec '…' is beyond a symbolic link`, rc 128). The loop reads the non-zero rc as "not ignored" and the gate goes red exactly when it has just been used — a false red naming a real-looking defect. Measured at this tip: `git check-ignore -q systemTest/playwright/results/latest-slot4` (the symlink ITSELF) is rc 0 both when the symlink exists and on a clean tree (the blanket `results/` rule at `systemTest/playwright/.gitignore:17` covers it), so probing the symlink itself removes the failure without weakening what is proven. **This task: E1 adds a two-line comment naming the rule; E2 changes the ONE probe line to the symlink itself; plus one NEW shell suite with two text reds, one behavioural red (the gate run with a `latest-slot4` symlink present), and three controls.** NOT in this task: the other five shapes, §6f2, any other block.

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# TESTS for Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-stack-safety.sh - latest-slot symlinks (KS-1093)
# =============================================================================
# The defect: with `systemTest/playwright/results/latest-slot4` a symlink,
# the gate prints `::error::latest-slot4/index.html is NOT gitignored on slot 4 (KS-682).`
# and exits 1 because `git check-ignore` refuses paths beyond a symbolic link.
# This suite proves E1+E2 fix that without weakening what is proven.
#
# Usage: bash Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/check_stack_safety_latest_slot_symlink.test.sh
# =============================================================================
set -uo pipefail
TOTAL_CELLS=6

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$HERE/../../../.." && pwd)"
SUBJ="${CHECK_STACK_SAFETY_SH-$REPO_ROOT/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-stack-safety.sh}"
[ -f "$SUBJ" ] || { echo "FATAL: check-stack-safety.sh not found at $SUBJ" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -r "$SUBJ" ] || { echo "FATAL: CHECK_STACK_SAFETY_SH is not readable at $SUBJ" >&2; exit 2; }
printf 'SUBJECT %s\n        sha256 %s\n\n' "$SUBJ" "$(shasum -a 256 "$SUBJ" | cut -d" " -f1)"

WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ks1093.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

pass=0; fail=0
ok()  { printf '  ok   %s\n' "$1"; pass=$((pass + 1)); }
bad() { printf '  FAIL %s\n     %s\n' "$1" "$2"; fail=$((fail + 1)); }
RES="$REPO_ROOT/systemTest/playwright/results"

# CELL 1 - RED at the tip: the through-symlink probe is gone.
through_hits="$(grep -c 'results/latest-slot${slot}/index.html' "$SUBJ" || true)"
if [ "$through_hits" -eq 0 ]; then ok "the probe no longer reads THROUGH the latest-slot symlink (index.html)"; else bad "the probe no longer reads THROUGH the latest-slot symlink (index.html)" "count=$through_hits (expected 0)"; fi
# CELL 2 - RED at the tip: the probe of the symlink itself is present.
self_hits="$(grep -c 'results/latest-slot${slot}"' "$SUBJ" || true)"
if [ "$self_hits" -eq 1 ]; then ok "the probe names the latest-slot symlink ITSELF"; else bad "the probe names the latest-slot symlink ITSELF" "count=$self_hits (expected 1)"; fi
# CELL 3 - CONTROL on a clean checkout: the gate exits 0 on this tree as found (nothing created yet).
bash "$SUBJ" > "$WORK/clean.out" 2>&1; rc_clean=$?
if [ "$rc_clean" -eq 0 ]; then ok "the gate exits 0 on this tree as found"; else bad "the gate exits 0 on this tree as found" "rc=$rc_clean: $(grep '::error::' "$WORK/clean.out" | head -2 | tr '\n' ' ')"; fi
# CELL 4 - RED at the tip: with a latest-slot4 SYMLINK present the gate still exits 0 and names no latest-slot error.
made_results=0; made_link=0
[ -d "$RES" ] || { mkdir -p "$RES"; made_results=1; }
if [ ! -e "$RES/latest-slot4" ] && [ ! -L "$RES/latest-slot4" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$RES/playwright-report-ks-1093-slot4"; : > "$RES/playwright-report-ks-1093-slot4/index.html"
  ln -s playwright-report-ks-1093-slot4 "$RES/latest-slot4"; made_link=1
fi
bash "$SUBJ" > "$WORK/symlink.out" 2>&1; rc_link=$?
link_errors="$(grep -c '::error::latest-slot' "$WORK/symlink.out" || true)"
if [ "$made_link" -eq 1 ]; then rm "$RES/latest-slot4"; rm "$RES/playwright-report-ks-1093-slot4/index.html"; rmdir "$RES/playwright-report-ks-1093-slot4"; fi
if [ "$made_results" -eq 1 ]; then rmdir "$RES" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
if [ "$rc_link" -eq 0 ] && [ "$link_errors" -eq 0 ]; then ok "with a latest-slot4 symlink present the gate exits 0 and names no latest-slot error"; else bad "with a latest-slot4 symlink present the gate exits 0 and names no latest-slot error" "rc=$rc_link latest-slot errors=$link_errors"; fi
# CELL 5 - CONTROL: the git mechanism the fix rests on, in a throwaway repo (through the symlink: rc 128; the symlink itself: rc 0).
git -C "$WORK" init -q; printf 'results/\n' > "$WORK/.gitignore"
mkdir -p "$WORK/results/playwright-report-x-slot4"; ln -s playwright-report-x-slot4 "$WORK/results/latest-slot4"
git -C "$WORK" check-ignore -q results/latest-slot4/index.html 2>/dev/null; rc_through=$?
git -C "$WORK" check-ignore -q results/latest-slot4 2>/dev/null; rc_self=$?
if [ "$rc_through" -eq 128 ] && [ "$rc_self" -eq 0 ]; then ok "git check-ignore refuses a path beyond a symlink (rc 128) and accepts the symlink itself (rc 0)"; else bad "git check-ignore refuses a path beyond a symlink (rc 128) and accepts the symlink itself (rc 0)" "through=$rc_through self=$rc_self"; fi
# CELL 6 - CONTROL: the subject parses.
if bash -n "$SUBJ" >/dev/null 2>&1; then ok "check-stack-safety.sh parses (bash -n)"; else bad "check-stack-safety.sh parses (bash -n)" "$(bash -n "$SUBJ" 2>&1 | head -5 | tr '\n' ' ')"; fi

printf '\n  %d passed, %d failed (of %d cells)\n' "$pass" "$fail" "$TOTAL_CELLS"
# A cell that never ran is not a pass (KS-1093 round 2): the ratio must add up.
if [ "$((pass + fail))" -ne "$TOTAL_CELLS" ]; then
  printf '  INCOMPLETE - %d of %d cells ran\n' "$((pass + fail))" "$TOTAL_CELLS"
  exit 1
fi
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
exit 0
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# CHECK: SHARED-STACK SAFETY INVARIANTS (KS-666)
# =============================================================================
# KS-666 made the destructive stack paths aware of what they are about to
# destroy, and namespaced stacks per slot. Almost all of that lives in shell
# scripts and compose YAML, where a well-meaning edit can silently undo it
# WITHOUT breaking anything visible: the stack still starts, the tests still
# pass, and the protection is simply gone until the next collision destroys
# someone's work.
#
# This is a static gate against exactly that. It asserts the STRUCTURE that
# makes the protection real, so a revert fails a PR instead of being noticed
# after the next incident.
#
# It deliberately duplicates nothing from the behavioural suites:
#   scripts/__tests__/stack_guard.test.sh  — what the guard DOES (17 cases)
#   scripts/__tests__/stack_env.test.sh    — the slot -> ports/project map (20)
# Those prove behaviour. This proves the behaviour is still WIRED IN.
#
# Usage: bash scripts/check-stack-safety.sh
# Exit 0 = all invariants hold; 1 = at least one has been reverted.
# =============================================================================

set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"   # Blockchain/Dev
# Repo root is TWO levels above Blockchain/Dev, not one — Blockchain/ is an
# intermediate directory, not the root. Resolve it via git so the check is
# correct regardless of where the tree is checked out or how deep it sits.
# NB the fallback MUST be grouped. `a || cd b && pwd` runs pwd even when a
# succeeds, because && binds to the result of the whole `a || cd b` list — which
# concatenated both paths into REPO and broke every path built from it.
REPO="$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || (cd "$ROOT/../.." && pwd))"

EXIT=0
CHECKS=0

fail() { echo "::error::$1"; shift; for l in "$@"; do echo "  $l"; done; EXIT=1; }
ok()   { CHECKS=$((CHECKS + 1)); }

# Assert a file contains a pattern.
must_contain() {
  local file="$1" pattern="$2" why="$3"
  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then
    fail "$file is missing — KS-666 protection removed." "$why"; return
  fi
  # `--` ends option parsing: a pattern starting with "--" (e.g. --filter ...)
  # is otherwise read by grep as an unrecognised option and never matches.
  if grep -qE -- "$pattern" "$file"; then ok; else
    fail "$file no longer matches /$pattern/ (KS-666)." "$why"
  fi
}

# Assert a file does NOT contain a pattern.
must_not_contain() {
  local file="$1" pattern="$2" why="$3"
  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then
    fail "$file is missing — KS-666 protection removed." "$why"; return
  fi
  local hits
  hits="$(grep -nE -- "$pattern" "$file" | grep -vE '^[0-9]+:\s*#' || true)"
  if [[ -z "$hits" ]]; then ok; else
    fail "$file matches forbidden /$pattern/ (KS-666)." "$why" "$hits"
  fi
}

COMPOSE="$ROOT/docker-compose.yml"
LOCAL_COMPOSE="$REPO/docker-compose.local.yml"
GUARD="$ROOT/scripts/stack_guard.sh"
ENVSH="$ROOT/scripts/stack_env.sh"
START="$REPO/Start_Up/start-secuura.sh"
STOP="$ROOT/stop-secuura.sh"
AKTO_START="$REPO/systemTest/akto/scripts/start.sh"
SLOT_TARGET="$REPO/systemTest/slot-target.sh"

# --- 1. The ownership marker ------------------------------------------------
# Without the marker the guard has nothing to read: it reports "no stack
# running" while 30+ containers are up, which is a FALSE ALL-CLEAR — strictly
# worse than no guard, because it actively reassures the operator.
must_contain "$COMPOSE" '^  stack-marker:' \
  "The marker keeps ownership readable when the rest of the stack is down — mid-build, mid-teardown, or with services stopped individually."
# Every service carries the labels too (the acceptance criterion). That the anchor exists is
# checked here; that it reaches every service is checked functionally by
# scripts/check-compose-stack-safety.mjs, which asks Compose for the resolved topology.
must_contain "$COMPOSE" '^x-stack-labels: &stack_labels' \
  "The ownership label anchor must exist so every service can merge it."
must_contain "$LOCAL_COMPOSE" '^x-stack-labels: &stack_labels' \
  "A YAML anchor cannot cross an include boundary, so each compose file needs its own."
for label in owner branch commit started_at; do
  must_contain "$COMPOSE" "com\.secuura\.stack\.${label}:" \
    "The guard prints and compares this label; dropping it blinds part of the refusal message."
done

# Required-variable syntax here would break every plain `docker compose config`,
# `ps` and both CI workflows for anyone who has not exported the vars.
must_not_contain "$COMPOSE" 'com\.secuura\.stack\.[a-z_]+: *"\$\{[A-Z_]+:\?' \
  "Use \${VAR:-unknown}, never \${VAR:?...}: required-variable syntax breaks plain compose invocations and CI."

# --- 2. The guard is actually invoked ---------------------------------------
# A guard that exists but is never called is decoration.
# Assert the filter is APPLIED, not merely that the label name appears. The
# string 'com.docker.compose.project' also occurs in the PROJECT_LABEL constant
# and in the other-stacks survey, so a looser pattern still passed after the
# filter line itself was deleted — the check claimed coverage it did not have.
must_contain "$GUARD" '--filter "label=\$\{PROJECT_LABEL\}=\$\{project\}"' \
  "The guard must filter its ownership read by compose project. Unscoped, docker ps returns newest-first and it reads the WRONG stack when two slots run."
must_contain "$GUARD" 'resolve_stack_project' \
  "The guard must resolve which project it is acting on before reading ownership labels."
must_contain "$START" 'stack_guard\.sh' \
  "start-secuura.sh must invoke the guard before its destructive paths."
must_contain "$START" 'run_stack_guard "stop the stack"' \
  "The --stop path must be guarded: stopping someone else's stack mid-run destroys their work in progress."
must_contain "$START" 'run_stack_guard "DESTROY all volumes' \
  "The --fresh-db path must be guarded — this is the path that caused the KS-666 near-miss."
must_contain "$START" 'run_stack_guard "rebuild all containers"' \
  "The --rebuild path must be guarded: it recreates every container under whoever is using the stack."
must_contain "$STOP" 'stack_guard\.sh' \
  "stop-secuura.sh must invoke the guard on BOTH its paths."

# --- 3. Both scripts agree on what a slot means -----------------------------
# stop-secuura.sh originally had no slot awareness, so from a slot-2 worktree it
# resolved the wrong project, stopped nothing, and printed "ALL SERVICES
# STOPPED". Sharing the derivation is what prevents that recurring.
must_contain "$ENVSH" 'SECUURA_STACK_SLOT' \
  "stack_env.sh is the single source of truth for slot -> ports/project/prefix."
# Anchor to an actual `source`/`.` command. Both scripts also carry a
# `# shellcheck source=...stack_env.sh` directive, so a bare filename match
# still passed after the real source line was deleted — mention, not use.
for f in "$START" "$STOP"; do
  must_contain "$f" '^[[:space:]]*(source|\.)[[:space:]]+.*stack_env\.sh' \
    "$(basename "$f") must SOURCE stack_env.sh so both scripts resolve the SAME compose project for a slot."
done

# Slot 1 must not be given a hardcoded project name: Compose derives it from the
# directory, and a guess would point the stack at a different project than every
# existing volume belongs to — an empty, healthy-looking stack.
must_contain "$ENVSH" 'if \(\( SECUURA_STACK_SLOT > 1 \)\); then' \
  "Slot 1 must leave COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME to Compose, or existing volumes are orphaned."

# --- 3b. start-secuura.sh probes the SLOT'S containers (KS-1096) -------------
# Sourcing stack_env.sh is not enough on its own: the script sourced it and still
# waited for, reported on and exec'd into slot 1's bare names (`secuura-postgres`,
# ...) and asked lsof about slot 1's 6432/6379 — so every slot >= 2 build ran the
# full 120 s health wait for nothing and printed "PostgreSQL not accepting /
# Redis not responding" under a Ready banner, exit 0. Nothing visible broke.
# Behaviour is proved by scripts/__tests__/start_secuura_slot_names.test.sh;
# this asserts the derivation is still wired in and the literals have not crept
# back. Comment lines are exempt (must_not_contain skips them), so the
# explanatory comments in the script itself do not trip these.
must_contain "$START" 'EXPECTED_SERVICES\+=\("\$\{STACK_PREFIX\}-' \
  "EXPECTED_SERVICES must be derived from STACK_PREFIX, or the health wait and --status look for slot 1's containers on every slot."
must_not_contain "$START" 'docker (exec|inspect)[[:space:]]+secuura-' \
  "A docker exec/inspect on a bare secuura-<svc> name targets slot 1's container from every slot; use \"\${STACK_PREFIX}-<svc>\"."
must_not_contain "$START" '^[[:space:]]*for port in .*(6432|6379)' \
  "The port pre-flight must use \$POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT / \$REDIS_EXTERNAL_PORT, not slot 1's literals."
for name in postgres redis; do
  must_contain "$START" 'docker exec "\$\{STACK_PREFIX\}-'"$name"'"' \
    "The ${name} connectivity probe must exec into this slot's container."
done

# --- 4. Volume destruction stays deliberate ---------------------------------
# `down -v` must appear exactly once, behind the --remove-volumes branch. Counting
# is used rather than pattern-matching the default path, because the legitimate
# guarded invocation and a reintroduced reflexive one look identical line-by-line.
dashv_count="$(grep -cE 'down -v' "$STOP" || true)"
if [[ "$dashv_count" == "1" ]] && grep -qE 'if \$REMOVE_VOLUMES; then' "$STOP"; then ok; else
  fail "stop-secuura.sh must use 'down -v' exactly once, inside the --remove-volumes branch (found ${dashv_count})." \
    "Volume destruction must always be a deliberate act, never the default teardown."
fi
must_contain "$STOP" 'docker compose ' \
  "Use compose v2 (docker compose), not the v1 docker-compose shim."
# Match the COMMAND, not the filename: `docker-compose.local.yml` legitimately
# contains the string, so require trailing whitespace to mean an invocation.
must_not_contain "$STOP" 'docker-compose[[:space:]]' \
  "docker-compose (v1) is banned; it also silently fails on hosts without the shim."

# The teardown must target the compose file the stack is actually STARTED from,
# or it stops a subset while reporting total success.
must_contain "$STOP" 'docker-compose\.local\.yml' \
  "stop-secuura.sh must target the root docker-compose.local.yml, which is what start-secuura.sh brings up."

# --- 5. Stack start-up must not write into the working tree -----------------
# This is what keeps the guard's uncommitted-changes check meaningful. If the
# tree is dirty as a matter of course, the check is permanently true and gets
# trained out within a week.
# Anchor to the start of a line so this matches the generator being INVOKED, not
# mentioned. The bootstrap's own advice message names the command in prose, and
# forbidding that would make the check unfixable without deleting the guidance.
must_not_contain "$AKTO_START" '^[[:space:]]*npm run generate-test-ids' \
  "Akto bootstrap must VERIFY (npm run check-test-ids), never regenerate into the tree — a permanently dirty tree makes the guard's dirty-tree check worthless."
must_not_contain "$AKTO_START" '^[[:space:]]*(npx )?prettier --write.*src/' \
  "Bootstrap must not format tracked files: that dirties the working tree on every start."
must_contain "$AKTO_START" 'npm run check-test-ids' \
  "The read-only catalog verification must stay in the bootstrap so drift is still reported."

# --- 6. Published ports ------------------------------------------------------
# Port offsetting is NOT asserted here any more. A grep for `- "1234:80"` cannot
# see a port that is parameterised but never offset — exactly the ollama
# (${OLLAMA_PORT:-11434}, profile local-llm) defect it missed. That property is
# now checked functionally by scripts/check-compose-stack-safety.mjs, which
# renders slot 1 and slot 2 with every profile enabled and asserts no published
# port is shared. This file only asserts that check still exists and is wired in.
must_contain "$ENVSH" 'OLLAMA_PORT=' \
  "Profile-gated services need offsetting too; ollama was parameterised but not offset."

# --- 6c. Shared slot numbering with platform-s (PS-622) ----------------------
# The two platforms use one stride and one numbering, so S slot N and K slot N pair up.
# platform-s exports STACK_SLOT; without honouring it, pairing needs two variables kept in
# sync by hand and a mismatch aims a suite at the wrong stack while looking healthy.
must_contain "$ENVSH" 'STACK_SLOT:-1' \
  "platform-k must accept platform-s's STACK_SLOT, or one export cannot drive both platforms."
must_contain "$ENVSH" 'SECUURA_MAX_STACK_SLOT=4' \
  "Four slots per platform is the agreed ceiling (PS-622); beyond it the allocations start to overlap."
# The registry and the script must agree on the ceiling, or one of them is lying.
if [[ "$(grep -oE '"maxSlots": *[0-9]+' "$ROOT/scripts/port-allocations.json" | grep -oE '[0-9]+')" == "4" ]]; then ok; else
  fail "port-allocations.json maxSlots must be 4, matching stack_env.sh (KS-666/PS-622)."
fi

# --- 6d. A requested slot must retarget a LOCAL url --------------------------
# systemTest/akto/.env.example ships SECUURA_API_URL=http://localhost:6882, so a configured
# value is often already present. If that always won, asking for slot 2 would silently leave
# the harness on slot 1 and the report would describe the wrong stack. platform-s hit this
# (PS-622) and found it only by running it.
must_contain "$SLOT_TARGET" '^is_local_url\(\)' \
  "slot-target.sh must distinguish local from remote urls, or a preset default defeats slot targeting."
must_contain "$SLOT_TARGET" '^retarget\(\)' \
  "A requested slot must retarget preset LOCAL urls; a remote target is a deliberate choice and stays."

# --- 6b. Harness targeting (KS-666) -----------------------------------------
# Every harness reads a DIFFERENT variable and all of them default to
# localhost:6882, so a harness that is not explicitly pointed somewhere tests
# slot 1 whichever slot you meant — and the report looks valid while describing
# the wrong system.
for v in SECUURA_BASE_URL GATEWAY_URL SECUURA_API_URL OVERRIDE_APP_URL PERF_BASE_URL; do
  must_contain "$SLOT_TARGET" "^export ${v}=" \
    "$v is how one of the four harnesses picks its target; without it that harness silently tests slot 1."
done
# Akto runs its OWN stack; sharing its mongo would put one slot's scan results
# into another slot's report.
must_contain "$SLOT_TARGET" '^export AKTO_COMPOSE_PROJECT=|AKTO_COMPOSE_PROJECT="\$\{AKTO_COMPOSE_PROJECT' \
  "Akto's side-stack must be namespaced per slot, or two runs share a mongo."
# An explicit `name:` in a compose file OVERRIDES project scoping, so namespacing
# the project alone left both slots on one mongo data directory.
must_contain "$SLOT_TARGET" 'AKTO_MONGO_VOLUME' \
  "Akto pins its volumes by explicit name, which defeats project scoping; they must be namespaced too."
# COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME overrides a compose file's own `name:`, so if it survives
# into a test shell every later compose command joins the PLATFORM's project — and
# an Akto teardown then removes the platform stack's containers as orphans.
must_contain "$SLOT_TARGET" '^unset COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME' \
  "The platform's compose project must not leak into a harness shell."
# Fixed report paths mean two concurrent runs overwrite each other, and the
# survivor describes a different stack than its filename implies.
PW_CONFIG="$REPO/Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts"
must_contain "$PW_CONFIG" 'SECUURA_ARTIFACT_SUFFIX' \
  "Playwright report paths must be slot-suffixed, or concurrent runs overwrite each other's results."
must_not_contain "$PW_CONFIG" "outputFolder: 'reports/html' \}" \
  "Playwright's html report path must not be fixed."

# --- 6e. The two HTML docs move with the tests -------------------------------
# secuura-test-discipline §4: every test change updates BOTH of platform-k's HTML docs in
# the same commit, never a follow-up — the flow diagram and the cheat sheet answer different
# questions, so updating one leaves the other actively misleading. This branch changes the
# systemTest estate substantially, and the docs were missed until the rule was re-read.
# Note the space in "Projects Documents": quote the path or the glob silently matches nothing
# and the check passes vacuously.
FLOW_DOC="$REPO/Projects Documents/API_Security_Functional_Testing_Architecture_Flow_Diagrams.html"
CHEAT_DOC="$REPO/Projects Documents/QA_Tool_Cheat_Sheet_Secuura_API_Testing.html"
for d in "$FLOW_DOC" "$CHEAT_DOC"; do
  if [[ ! -f "$d" ]]; then
    fail "$(basename "$d") is missing — platform-k's test docs must exist (secuura-test-discipline §4)."
  elif grep -q 'SECUURA_STACK_SLOT' "$d"; then ok; else
    fail "$(basename "$d") does not document the stack slots (KS-666)." \
      "Both HTML docs must describe how a suite is pointed at a slot and where its results land;" \
      "one updated and one not is worse than neither, because the stale one reads as current."
  fi
done

# --- 6f. Test results must never reach the repo ------------------------------
# Slot-labelled runs are named <name>-<ticket>-slot<N>, and a bare `test-results/` pattern
# matches only the exact historic name — so every labelled run left an untracked directory
# behind, and two were committed by accident. That matters beyond tidiness: a permanently
# dirty tree is what makes the guard's uncommitted-changes check worthless.
# KS-674: the per-slot auth directories are on this list too, and they are the one entry where a
# miss is a SECURITY problem rather than an untidy tree — `.auth-<ticket>-slot<N>/token.json`
# holds a live bearer token, and `.auth/` does not match it any more than `test-results/` matched
# `test-results-ks-666-slot1/`.
# Each path below names a FILE inside the artifact directory, never the bare directory.
# `git check-ignore` matches a trailing-slash pattern against a directory only once that
# directory exists on disk, so checking the bare name passed on a machine that had just run
# the suite and failed on a clean checkout — including CI. A file path matches the pattern
# whether or not anything exists.
for artifact in \
  "$REPO/Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/test-results-ks-666-slot1/.last-run.json" \
  "$REPO/Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/reports/results-ks-666-slot1.json" \
  "$REPO/systemTest/akto/output/reports-slot2/report.html" \
  "$REPO/systemTest/performance/reports/performance-reports/run/summary.json" \
  "$REPO/systemTest/playwright/results/playwright-report-ks-666-slot1/index.html" \
  "$REPO/systemTest/playwright/results/test-results-ks-666-slot1/.last-run.json" \
  "$REPO/.schemathesis/default/cache.json" \
  "$REPO/systemTest/playwright/.auth-ks-666-slot3/token.json" \
  "$REPO/systemTest/schemathesis/.env-ks-666-slot3"; do
  if git -C "$REPO" check-ignore -q "$artifact" 2>/dev/null; then ok; else
    fail "$(basename "$artifact") is NOT gitignored (KS-666)." \
      "Slot-labelled results must never reach the repo. Add a pattern that matches the" \
      "suffixed name, not just the historic one — 'test-results/' does not cover" \
      "'test-results-ks-666-slot1/'."
  fi
done

# KS-682: the Playwright artefact shapes, DERIVED for every slot rather than hand-picked for one.
# Since KS-682 a run writes `results/<name>-<ticket>-<ISO>-slot<N>/` behind a `results/latest-slot<N>`
# pointer and reads `.auth-<ticket>-slot<N>/`. An earlier version of this check probed a single real
# run's timestamp on slot 1 and a bare `latest-slot3` — one instance each, and the bare name broke
# the rule above. The stamp here is deliberately synthetic (it is a shape, not a run), and the loop
# covers slots 1-4 so a pattern that happens to match one slot's spelling cannot pass for all.
#
# Honest limit, measured on #803 review: `systemTest/playwright/.gitignore` carries a blanket
# `results/`, so every `results/...` probe passes by that line alone — they prove the blanket
# holds, not the suffix. The `.auth-*/` probe is the one that tests a suffix pattern, and it is the
# one holding a bearer token, which is why it is here for every slot and not just slot 3.
PW_STAMP="2026-01-01T00-00-00-000Z"
for slot in 1 2 3 4; do
  for artifact in \
    "$REPO/systemTest/playwright/results/playwright-report-ks-682-${PW_STAMP}-slot${slot}/index.html" \
    "$REPO/systemTest/playwright/results/test-results-ks-682-${PW_STAMP}-slot${slot}/.last-run.json" \
    "$REPO/systemTest/playwright/results/har-ks-682-${PW_STAMP}-slot${slot}/1.har" \
    "$REPO/systemTest/playwright/results/latest-slot${slot}/index.html" \
    "$REPO/systemTest/playwright/.auth-ks-682-slot${slot}/token.json" \
    "$REPO/systemTest/playwright/.auth-ks-682-slot${slot}/state.json"; do
    if git -C "$REPO" check-ignore -q "$artifact" 2>/dev/null; then ok; else
      fail "$(basename "$(dirname "$artifact")")/$(basename "$artifact") is NOT gitignored on slot ${slot} (KS-682)." \
        "Every per-slot Playwright artefact shape must be ignored on every slot; a pattern that" \
        "matches one slot's spelling is the KS-666 defect again."
    fi
  done
done

# --- 6f2. No hardcoded slot-1 container names in harness source ----------------
# KS-666: `preflight.ts` and `engineDiagnostics.ts` each hardcoded `akto-testing` — slot 1's
# container. On slot 4 the container is `akto-s4-testing`, so `docker exec akto-testing` failed
# on a container that does not exist and pre-flight reported "the Secuura target is not
# reachable", blaming the platform for a name the harness got wrong.
#
# KS-687 F2: the inline check that lived here could not see F1 (`scripts/dump-result-fields.sh`
# resolving `${AKTO_MONGO_CONTAINER:-akto-mongo}`) on two axes at once — corpus (src/bin, *.ts) and
# pattern (literals only; F1 was a DEFAULTED variable) — and its ">= 10 files" non-vacuity assert
# passed over the missing directory because a count measures volume, not coverage. The check is
# now `check-akto-container-names.sh`: wider corpus (+ scripts/, + *.sh/*.mjs), the defaulted-
# variable shape in shell and TS, and a coverage assert that names each (dir, extension) the corpus
# must contribute and fails on the first that is absent. It is exercised red-first by
# `__tests__/check_akto_container_names.test.sh` (F1's original line is the first fixture).
# Exit 2 (corpus incomplete) is a failure here, not a skip: a negative from a partial corpus is
# exactly the reassurance F2 was filed about.
akto_gate="$ROOT/scripts/check-akto-container-names.sh"
if [[ ! -f "$akto_gate" ]]; then
  fail "$akto_gate is missing — KS-687 F2 gate removed."
else
  akto_out="$(bash "$akto_gate" "$REPO/systemTest/akto" 2>&1)"; akto_rc=$?
  case "$akto_rc" in
    0) ok ;;
    2) fail "Akto container-name gate could not scan a complete corpus (KS-687 F2)."          "A 'no hits' over a partial corpus is not a clean result:" "$akto_out" ;;
    *) fail "Akto container-name gate found a violation (KS-666 / KS-687 F2)." "$akto_out" ;;
  esac
fi

# --- 6g. A slot runs one suite at a time --------------------------------------
# Slots run in parallel with each other; suites within a slot do not. Two harnesses on one
# slot contend for the same gateway, database and seeded state — Akto replays traffic while
# k6 measures latency, so the performance figures describe a stack under someone else's load.
# Neither errors; both measure something nobody asked about.
must_contain "$REPO/systemTest/run-in-slot.sh" 'mkdir "\$LOCK"' \
  "The per-slot lock must be an atomic mkdir; a check-then-create races exactly when it matters."

# --- 7. The behavioural suites still exist ----------------------------------
# KS-682: docker-compose.tokenomics.yml must be slot-aware. It hard-coded "8881:80" and the
# container name while docker-compose.local.yml declared the same service through
# ${TOKENOMICS_PORT:-8881} / ${STACK_PREFIX:-secuura}, so brought up beside any other slot it bound
# slot 1's port and name and the second one failed to start. check-compose-stack-safety.mjs reads
# only docker-compose.local.yml, so this file had no gate — found on the four-slot live sweep.
TOK="$REPO/docker-compose.tokenomics.yml"
if grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*"8881:80"' "$TOK" || grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*container_name:[[:space:]]*secuura-tokenomics-website[[:space:]]*$' "$TOK"; then
  fail "docker-compose.tokenomics.yml hard-codes slot 1's tokenomics port or container name (KS-682)" \
       "Use \${TOKENOMICS_PORT:-8881}:80 and \${STACK_PREFIX:-secuura}-tokenomics-website, as docker-compose.local.yml does."
else ok; fi
if ! grep -q 'TOKENOMICS_PORT:-8881' "$TOK" || ! grep -q 'STACK_PREFIX:-secuura' "$TOK"; then
  fail "docker-compose.tokenomics.yml no longer derives its port and container name from the slot (KS-682)"
else ok; fi

# KS-682 (carried from KS-971): the auth service must be handed ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD. It is
# templated in .env.example:133 and read by the seeder, but until 2026-09-10 no compose file
# forwarded it — so the value an operator set was inert, admin@secuura.com was never seeded on a
# fresh local stack, the bootstrap admin could not grant roles, and every harness fell back to
# an account that 401s (KS-972). The `:-` default is load-bearing: it makes an UNSET host value
# arrive as '' and take the seeder's fail-closed null branch, rather than being absent.
COMPOSE="$ROOT/docker-compose.yml"
if awk '/^  auth:$/{in_auth=1; next} /^  [a-z][a-z0-9-]*:$/{in_auth=0} in_auth' "$COMPOSE" \
     | grep -qE '^\s*-\s*ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD=\$\{ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD:-\}\s*$'; then ok; else
  fail "docker-compose.yml's auth service no longer forwards ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD (KS-682 / KS-972)" \
       "Add '- ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD=\${ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD:-}' to the auth environment block. Without it" \
       "the seeder never sees the value, admin@secuura.com is never seeded, and provisioning cannot" \
       "grant roles on a fresh stack."
fi

for t in "$ROOT/scripts/__tests__/stack_guard.test.sh" "$ROOT/scripts/__tests__/stack_env.test.sh" \
         "$ROOT/scripts/__tests__/stop_secuura.test.sh" "$ROOT/scripts/check-compose-stack-safety.mjs" \
         "$ROOT/scripts/check-port-crossover.mjs" "$ROOT/scripts/port-allocations.json" \
         "$REPO/systemTest/slot-target.sh" "$REPO/systemTest/__tests__/slot_target.test.sh" \
         "$REPO/systemTest/run-in-slot.sh" "$REPO/systemTest/__tests__/run_in_slot.test.sh" \
         "$REPO/systemTest/__tests__/manifest_path.test.sh" \
         "$REPO/systemTest/__tests__/provision_base_url.test.sh" \
         "$ROOT/scripts/__tests__/check_akto_container_names.test.sh"; do
  if [[ -f "$t" ]]; then ok; else
    fail "$(basename "$t") is missing — KS-666's behavioural coverage was deleted."
  fi
done

if [[ $EXIT -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo "OK — ${CHECKS} shared-stack safety invariants hold (KS-666)."
fi
exit $EXIT

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# TESTS for Blockchain/Dev/scripts/docker-build.sh — an EMPTY SERVICES_TABLE
# (KS-877)
# =============================================================================
# The defect: with an empty SERVICES_TABLE, `docker-build.sh all` died at the
# banner's `${BUILD_LIST[*]}` with `BUILD_LIST[*]: unbound variable` under
# bash 3.2 + `set -u` — three lines after the `[ -n ]` guard added for exactly
# this class. That guard works (BUILD_LIST is left genuinely empty); the display
# expansion after it does not. And `${BUILD_LIST[*]:-}` alone only moves the
# death 55 lines down to the parallel loop's `"${BUILD_LIST[@]}"` — measured —
# so the shape that holds is a guard on `${#BUILD_LIST[@]}` that names the
# table and exits before either.
#
# docker is NEVER run: a stub on a private PATH records every call and exits 0,
# so the control cells can prove the working path still builds without a
# daemon. The empty table is produced by a fixture COPY of the subject whose
# heredoc body is stripped — the table is a literal inside the script, so
# there is no other way to reach the path — and the copy's row count is
# asserted 29 -> 0 before the cell is scored.
#
# Round 2 (KS-877, the tier-2 gate's F1): CELL 3 was RED on the repository's CI
# (ubuntu, bash 5.x) while green on macOS — `docker-build.sh`'s `((RUNNING++))`
# exits 1 when RUNNING is 0, and bash >= 4.1 `set -e` (COMPAT item 45) kills the
# script on it; bash 3.2 does not. CELL 4 pins the construct's ABSENCE statically
# (this box has no bash >= 4.1; CI's CELL 3 is the runtime instrument) and CELL 5
# proves the fix does not swallow a genuine build failure. The summary line
# carries the cell count (`(of N cells)`) and the run FAILS if fewer cells ran.
#
# Usage: bash Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/docker_build_empty_table.test.sh
#        DOCKER_BUILD_SH=/path/to/other/docker-build.sh bash …   (red-proof)
# =============================================================================
set -uo pipefail
TOTAL_CELLS=5

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$HERE/../../../.." && pwd)"
# Same subject discipline as orchestrate_jobs.test.sh (KS-923 F2 / KS-941).
if [ "${DOCKER_BUILD_SH+set}" = set ] && [ -z "$DOCKER_BUILD_SH" ]; then
  echo "FATAL: DOCKER_BUILD_SH is set but EMPTY — refusing to silently grade the shipped script." >&2
  exit 2
fi
SUBJ="${DOCKER_BUILD_SH-$REPO_ROOT/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/docker-build.sh}"
[ -f "$SUBJ" ] || { echo "FATAL: docker-build.sh not found at $SUBJ" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -r "$SUBJ" ] || { echo "FATAL: DOCKER_BUILD_SH is not readable at $SUBJ" >&2; exit 2; }
printf 'SUBJECT %s\n        sha256 %s\n\n' "$SUBJ" "$(shasum -a 256 "$SUBJ" | cut -d" " -f1)"

WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ks877.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

pass=0; fail=0
ok()  { printf '  ok   %s\n' "$1"; pass=$((pass + 1)); }
bad() { printf '  FAIL %s\n     %s\n' "$1" "$2"; fail=$((fail + 1)); }

# Data rows of the SERVICES_TABLE heredoc in a script: tab-separated, not a
# comment. The same predicate service_names() applies.
table_rows() {
  sed -n "/^SERVICES_TABLE=\"\$(cat <<'SERVICES_EOF'\$/,/^SERVICES_EOF\$/p" "$1" \
    | awk -F'\t' 'NF==2 && $1 !~ /^[[:space:]]*#/' | wc -l | tr -d ' '
}

# Build a fixture project root around a copy of the script under test.
#   $1 = dir   $2 = table: intact | emptied
# The copy lives at <root>/scripts/docker-build.sh so the script's own
# `PROJECT_ROOT="$SCRIPT_DIR/.."` resolves to the fixture root.
build_fixture() {
  local root="$1" table="$2"
  rm -rf "$root"; mkdir -p "$root/scripts" "$root/bin" "$root/services/auth"
  printf 'FROM scratch\n' > "$root/services/auth/Dockerfile"
  if [ "$table" = emptied ]; then
    # Strip every line between the heredoc's opening and closing markers.
    sed "/^SERVICES_TABLE=\"\$(cat <<'SERVICES_EOF'\$/,/^SERVICES_EOF\$/{//!d;}" "$SUBJ" > "$root/scripts/docker-build.sh"
  else
    cp "$SUBJ" "$root/scripts/docker-build.sh"
  fi
  # docker stub: records every call, succeeds.
  { printf '#!/bin/bash\n'; printf 'echo "docker $*" >> "%s/docker_calls.txt"\nexit 0\n' "$root"; } > "$root/bin/docker"
  chmod +x "$root/bin/docker"
}

# Run the copy with ONLY the stub dir in front of the system dirs. Prints rc.
run_build() {
  local root="$1"; shift
  ( export PATH="$root/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"; cd "$root" && bash scripts/docker-build.sh "$@" ) >"$root/out.txt" 2>&1
  echo $?
}
build_calls() { if [ -f "$1/docker_calls.txt" ]; then grep -c '^docker build' "$1/docker_calls.txt" || true; else echo 0; fi; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 1 — KS-877. THE REGRESSION. An EMPTY table must be refused by name —
# "no services matched", naming SERVICES_TABLE — with NO `unbound variable`
# and no build attempted. Asserted on rc = 1 AND the ABSENCE of the
# unbound-variable death AND the PRESENCE of the message naming SERVICES_TABLE
# AND 0 builds. rc alone cannot discriminate base from head (both exit 1),
# which is why the other three clauses exist; it is asserted so that a guard
# that prints the message and then exits 0 still reds (the gate's Tk). The row
# count is a precondition: a copy that still has rows would pass the pre-fix
# script and say nothing.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/empty" emptied
rows_subj="$(table_rows "$SUBJ")"; rows_copy="$(table_rows "$WORK/empty/scripts/docker-build.sh")"
if [ "$rows_subj" -lt 1 ] || [ "$rows_copy" -ne 0 ]; then
  bad "an EMPTY SERVICES_TABLE is refused by name with no 'unbound variable'" \
      "precondition broken: subject rows=$rows_subj (expected >=1), emptied copy rows=$rows_copy (expected 0) — the cell cannot discriminate"
else
  rc_empty="$(run_build "$WORK/empty" all)"
  if [ "$rc_empty" = 1 ] && ! grep -q 'unbound variable' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" \
     && grep -q 'no services matched' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" && grep -q 'SERVICES_TABLE' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" \
     && [ "$(build_calls "$WORK/empty")" -eq 0 ]; then
    ok "an EMPTY SERVICES_TABLE ($rows_subj rows -> $rows_copy) is refused by name — 'no services matched', naming SERVICES_TABLE — with no 'unbound variable', 0 builds, rc=$rc_empty"
  else
    bad "an EMPTY SERVICES_TABLE is refused by name with no 'unbound variable'" \
        "rc=$rc_empty, unbound variable present=$(grep -q 'unbound variable' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" && echo YES || echo no), message present=$(grep -q 'no services matched' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" && echo yes || echo NO), table named=$(grep -q 'SERVICES_TABLE' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" && echo yes || echo NO), builds=$(build_calls "$WORK/empty"), last lines: $(tail -2 "$WORK/empty/out.txt" | sed 's|.*/scripts/||' | tr '\n' ' ')"
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 2 — CONTROL (the working path, one service). The intact table with
# `auth` must still print `Services:  auth`, build it once via the stub, report
# BUILD OK and exit 0. Without this, CELL 1 could pass by a guard that refuses
# every list.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/one" intact
rc_one="$(run_build "$WORK/one" auth)"
if [ "$rc_one" = 0 ] && grep -q '^  Services:  auth$' "$WORK/one/out.txt" && grep -q '\[auth\] BUILD OK' "$WORK/one/out.txt" \
   && [ "$(build_calls "$WORK/one")" -eq 1 ] && grep -q -- '-f services/auth/Dockerfile' "$WORK/one/docker_calls.txt"; then
  ok "CONTROL — the intact table with 'auth' prints 'Services:  auth', builds it once (-f services/auth/Dockerfile), BUILD OK, rc 0"
else
  bad "CONTROL — the intact table with 'auth' still builds it once and exits 0" \
      "rc=$rc_one, builds=$(build_calls "$WORK/one"), output: $(grep -v '^=*$' "$WORK/one/out.txt" | tail -4 | tr '\n' ' ')"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 3 — CONTROL (the working path, every service, the parallel loop). The
# intact table with `all` must build every row via the stub and exit 0 — the
# path whose re-index guard (`${#PIDS[@]}`) the file's own comment documents,
# exercised under bash 3.2 with instant builds so the loop's empty-array case
# is actually reached.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/all" intact
rc_all="$(run_build "$WORK/all" all)"
if [ "$rc_all" = 0 ] && grep -q "SUCCEEDED ($rows_subj):" "$WORK/all/out.txt" && grep -q 'All builds succeeded' "$WORK/all/out.txt" \
   && [ "$(build_calls "$WORK/all")" -eq "$rows_subj" ] && ! grep -q 'unbound variable' "$WORK/all/out.txt"; then
  ok "CONTROL — the intact table with 'all' builds every row ($rows_subj stub builds), SUCCEEDED ($rows_subj), rc 0, no unbound variable"
else
  bad "CONTROL — the intact table with 'all' builds every row and exits 0" \
      "rc=$rc_all, builds=$(build_calls "$WORK/all") of $rows_subj, output: $(grep -i 'unbound\|SUCCEEDED\|FAILED' "$WORK/all/out.txt" | head -3 | tr '\n' ' ')"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 4 — KS-877 round 2 (the gate's F1). The subject has NO bare
# arithmetic-command post-increment/decrement (`((X++))` / `((X--))` on a line
# of its own). Such a command exits 1 when its expression evaluates to 0 — a
# post-increment yields the OLD value, so `((RUNNING++))` at RUNNING=0 "fails"
# — and bash >= 4.1 `set -e` exits on it (bash COMPAT item 45: "Bash-4.1 …
# exits when any command fails, not just a simple command or pipeline").
# bash 3.2 (macOS) does not, which is why CELL 3 was green here and RED on CI's
# ubuntu (run 34743050388: `rc=1, builds=0 of 29` — the script died after
# backgrounding ONE build). This is a STATIC pin, honest about being one: the
# runtime pin is CELL 3 on a bash >= 4.1, i.e. CI. The positive control inside
# the cell proves the grep can fire (a here-string holding `((X++))` -> 1).
# `[[:space:]]`, not `\s`: BSD grep.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ARITH_RE='^[[:space:]]*\(\([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*(\+\+|--)\)\)[[:space:]]*$'
arith_control="$(printf '  ((X++))\n' | grep -cE "$ARITH_RE" || true)"
arith_hits="$(grep -nE "$ARITH_RE" "$SUBJ" || true)"
arith_count="$(printf '%s' "$arith_hits" | grep -c . || true)"
if [ "$arith_control" != 1 ]; then
  bad "the subject has NO bare arithmetic-command post-increment/decrement" \
      "instrument cannot fire: the positive control read $arith_control (expected 1) — the cell is not scoring the subject"
elif [ "$arith_count" -eq 0 ]; then
  ok "the subject has NO bare arithmetic-command post-increment/decrement — ((X++)) exits 1 at 0 and bash >= 4.1 set -e dies on it (control fires: $arith_control)"
else
  bad "the subject has NO bare arithmetic-command post-increment/decrement" \
      "count=$arith_count (control=$arith_control): $(printf '%s' "$arith_hits" | sed 's/^\([0-9]*\):[[:space:]]*/:\1 /' | tr '\n' ' ')"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 5 — KS-877 round 2, the MASK CONTROL. A run where ONE build genuinely
# fails must still land in `FAILED (1)` with rc 1 and the summary printed —
# the counter fix must not swallow a real failure. A second stub records the
# call, then exits 1 when its args name services/auth/Dockerfile (asserted
# unique among the table's rows). On bash 3.2 this reads the SAME before and
# after the fix — that IS the control: the fix changes nothing 3.2 can see
# except the arithmetic status; on CI (bash 5.x) it exercises the fixed loop
# under a genuine failure.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/onefail" intact
{ printf '#!/bin/bash\n'; printf 'echo "docker $*" >> "%s/docker_calls.txt"\ncase "$*" in *services/auth/Dockerfile*) exit 1;; esac\nexit 0\n' "$WORK/onefail"; } > "$WORK/onefail/bin/docker"
chmod +x "$WORK/onefail/bin/docker"
auth_rows="$(sed -n "/^SERVICES_TABLE=\"\$(cat <<'SERVICES_EOF'\$/,/^SERVICES_EOF\$/p" "$WORK/onefail/scripts/docker-build.sh" \
  | awk -F'\t' 'NF==2 && $1 !~ /^[[:space:]]*#/ && $2 == "services/auth/Dockerfile"' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
if [ "$auth_rows" -ne 1 ]; then
  bad "MASK CONTROL — one genuinely failing build still lands in FAILED (1), rc 1" \
      "precondition broken: $auth_rows table rows resolve to services/auth/Dockerfile (expected exactly 1) — the failing stub cannot be aimed"
else
  rc_onefail="$(run_build "$WORK/onefail" all)"
  if [ "$rc_onefail" = 1 ] && grep -q "SUCCEEDED ($((rows_subj - 1))):" "$WORK/onefail/out.txt" && grep -q 'FAILED (1):' "$WORK/onefail/out.txt" \
     && grep -q '^    auth$' "$WORK/onefail/out.txt" && ! grep -q 'All builds succeeded' "$WORK/onefail/out.txt" \
     && [ "$(build_calls "$WORK/onefail")" -eq "$rows_subj" ] && ! grep -q 'unbound variable' "$WORK/onefail/out.txt"; then
    ok "MASK CONTROL — with the auth stub exiting 1, 'all' still runs every row ($rows_subj stub builds), SUCCEEDED ($((rows_subj - 1))), FAILED (1): auth, rc 1"
  else
    bad "MASK CONTROL — one genuinely failing build still lands in FAILED (1), rc 1" \
        "rc=$rc_onefail, builds=$(build_calls "$WORK/onefail") of $rows_subj, output: $(grep -i 'unbound\|SUCCEEDED\|FAILED\|All builds' "$WORK/onefail/out.txt" | head -4 | tr '\n' ' ')"
  fi
fi

printf '\n  %d passed, %d failed (of %d cells)\n' "$pass" "$fail" "$TOTAL_CELLS"
# A cell that never ran is not a pass (KS-877 round 2): the ratio must add up.
if [ "$((pass + fail))" -ne "$TOTAL_CELLS" ]; then
  printf '  INCOMPLETE — %d of %d cells ran\n' "$((pass + fail))" "$TOTAL_CELLS"
  exit 1
fi
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
exit 0
